about: IIT Delhi began in 1959 as the College of Engineering in Hauz Khas, becoming a full Institute of Technology under a 1963 Act of Parliament, and today runs sixteen engineering and science departments alongside newer schools in artificial intelligence, biological sciences and public policy. Named an Institution of Eminence in 2018, it has placed among India's top two or three engineering institutes in NIRF for several years and cracked the QS World top-120 for 2027. It recently opened a second campus at Sonipat, Haryana, alongside an overseas campus in Abu Dhabi.

location.nearestAirport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi
location.nearestRailway: New Delhi Railway Station, about 10-15 km
location.connectivityNote: The Hauz Khas campus sits in south Delhi, next to the Hauz Khas Metro station. Indira Gandhi International Airport is roughly 15-20 km away by road, and New Delhi Railway Station, the city's main railhead, is about 10-15 km away. IIT Delhi also runs a newer campus at Sonipat, Haryana, outside the capital, and an overseas campus in Abu Dhabi.

admissionRoutes.note: Admission to B.Tech and the 5-year B.Tech+M.Tech Dual Degree programmes, including the B.Tech in Design, runs through JEE (Advanced) rank with seats allotted via JoSAA counselling.

admissionRoutes.note: M.Tech and MS (Research) admission is based on a qualifying national exam such as GATE or JAM, per the requirements each academic unit sets for its programme.
The MBA at the Department of Management Studies admits through the CAT score, followed by a group discussion and personal interview.

Ph.D admission runs through the concerned Department/Centre/School, which typically combines a written test and/or interview and may set extra requirements for its own academic goals, separate from JEE-based UG admission.
